problem:
Given that the expression $2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-5\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)$ can be written as $R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-ϕ)$ with ${0}^{∘}<ϕ<{90}^{∘}$ and $R>0,$ what is the **exact** value of $ϕ?$

$ϕ=\operatorname{arctan}⁡($ 
{{field-1}} $)$
worked_solution:
The difference formula for sine gives

$$
\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-ϕ) & =R(\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ-\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ) \\  & =R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, by writing the given expression in the amplitude-phase form

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-5\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=R\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x-ϕ),
$$

we get the following identity:

$$
2\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-5\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)=(R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)-(R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ)\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x)
$$

Equating the coefficients of $\operatorname{sin}⁡(3x)$ and $\operatorname{cos}⁡(3x),$ we get the following system of equations:

$$
{\begin{aligned}R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ=2 \\ R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ=5\end{aligned}
$$

Dividing the second equation by the first, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{R\operatorname{sin}⁡ϕ}{R\operatorname{cos}⁡ϕ} & =\frac{5}{2} \\ \operatorname{tan}⁡ϕ & =\frac{5}{2} \\ ϕ & =\operatorname{arctan}⁡(\frac{5}{2}).\end{aligned}
$$
